content:
Alex, Jamie, and [Sofia](/note/people/sofia_rossi) walked from the harbor steps to
the pocket garden using the [conversation kit](/note/notes/interview_kit).

![Illustration of a quiet pocket garden with tall grasses, a curved bench, and a neighborhood path](assets/images/pocket-garden-field-day.webp)

*A fictional field-day scene. The goal is to notice the conditions for welcome,
not to rate a place or its visitors.*

## 09:10 — Harbor steps

The strongest signal was not the view but the movable chairs. People made
temporary circles, then returned the chairs to the wall. A tiny ritual of care.

## 10:25 — Bakery window

A water bowl and a hand-drawn notice created more conversation than the polished
signage. This supports the “invite, do not rank” principle in
[Design principles](/note/notes/design_principles).

## 11:40 — Pocket garden

There was a genuine quiet corner behind the tall grasses. Sofia noted that the
garden feels social without requiring participation—a useful nuance for
[third-place research](/note/notes/research/third_places).

Next: [synthesize the interviews](/note/tasks/synthesize_interviews) before the
weekly [research roundtable](/note/events/2026/research_roundtable).
